say.en: Between 1960 and 2000, India's wheat output rose from about 11 to 75 million tonnes, largely thanks to new high-yielding, semi-dwarf varieties produced by plant breeders. In this lesson: List the main steps of plant breeding.
Describe breeding for disease and insect resistance.
Explain biofortification.

body.en: *Plant breeding* changes the heredity of a crop to give better plants. The steps are: (1) collection of variability from wild relatives and cultivars (germplasm collection); (2) evaluation and selection of parents; (3) cross hybridisation of the chosen parents; (4) selection and testing of superior recombinants over several generations; (5) testing, release and commercialisation after field trials in many locations. Breeders aim at higher yield, disease and pest resistance, tolerance to stress, and better quality.

body.en: Breeding for disease *resistance* uses resistant parents found in germplasm or made by mutation (by chemicals or radiation), e.g. wheat Himgiri (resistant to leaf and stripe rust), Brassica Pusa Swarnim (white rust), cowpea Pusa Komal (bacterial blight). Insect resistance comes from morphological traits (hairy leaves of cotton against jassids), or biochemical ones (high aspartic acid, low nitrogen and sugar in maize against stem borers). Biofortification breeds crops with more vitamins, minerals or better proteins, e.g. maize with twice the lysine and tryptophan, iron-rich rice and vitamin-rich vegetables.

points.en: Insect *resistance*: hairy leaves, solid stems, chemistry
Biofortification: more nutrients in the crop

problem.en: In a maize field the mean height is 180 cm. Plants with a mean height of 200 cm are chosen as parents, and their offspring average 186 cm. Find the heritability of height.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. In a maize field the mean height is 180 cm. Plants with a mean height of 200 cm are chosen as parents, and their offspring average 186 cm. Find the heritability of height.

say.en: Let us solve this together. In a maize field the mean height is 180 centimetres. Plants with a mean height of 200 centimetres are chosen as parents, and their offspring average 186 centimetres. Find the heritability of height.
S equals 200 minus 180 equals 20 centimetres; R equals 186 minus 180 equals 6 centimetres.
h squared equals R over S equals 6 over 20 equals 0.3.
So the answer is h squared equals 0.3.
